scope: Current factual package for the members-only Guardians of the Rift Runecraft minigame. It is integration-ready research only: it proposes facts, actions, graph records, and explicit account observations without changing production data, assigning route order, scoring the activity, or treating community targets as facts.

included: current quest, skill, item, location, transport, reward, and shop mechanics
deterministic versus random acquisition and consumption boundaries
round phases, energy caps, point rounding, threshold, failure, and session-item behavior
fixed utility of the outfit, ring, pouch, lantern, talismans, and cosmetic rewards
current official August 2026 needle, lantern, and Guardian's Eye changes
proposed observation fields that require player-reported values
excluded: whether this activity should be done early or for how long
XP, rune, pearl, search, or game-per-hour estimates as account facts
a recommended pearl purchase order or stop condition
assumed account readiness, round success, earned energy, points, searches, RNG drops, or collection-log state

energy_and_contribution.guardian_stone: Each ordinary elemental or catalytic guardian stone gives 2 energy of its matching type and 5 Runecraft XP when used on the Great Guardian. A combination-rune polyelemental stone gives 3 elemental energy.
energy_and_contribution.cell_actions: Building, recharging, and strengthening barriers award equal elemental and catalytic energy. Creating a guardian awards only its alignment's energy. Building a barrier always awards 2 of each energy; higher-tier cells otherwise give more. The current full-barrier cell contribution cap is 2,500 Runecraft XP and 450 energy per game.
energy_and_contribution.repair: Repairing a broken cell tile consumes 12 guardian fragments and gives 25 elemental plus 25 catalytic energy.
energy_and_contribution.caps: Maximum total energy is 1,200 per game, or 1,320 with a lantern burning yew logs. Each energy type is capped at 1,000. Reaching a cap prevents further energy until the rift closes.
energy_and_contribution.mining_xp_boundary: Guardian-fragment Mining XP is capped after the first 250 fragments mined in a game; mined amount is not inferred.

completion_or_reward_events.event: successful round with at least 300 total energy personally gained
completion_or_reward_events.deterministic_formula: end-of-round Runecraft XP = current Runecraft level x 45
completion_or_reward_events.point_formula: one elemental point per 100 elemental energy and one catalytic point per 100 catalytic energy; every fractional hundred independently has an equal-percent chance to round up
completion_or_reward_events.state_rule: never compute, grant, or infer XP, energy, points, searches, or a successful round without player-reported observations

completion_or_reward_events.requirements: spend exactly one elemental point and one catalytic point; Big-Search spends five of each for five independent searches
completion_or_reward_events.state_rule: a search count and each result are player-observed; neither follows just from activity completion

completion_or_reward_events.requirements: spend exactly 25 abyssal pearls to receive one elemental point and one catalytic point, sufficient for one search
completion_or_reward_events.state_rule: deterministic only after an observed 25-pearl balance; it does not grant a reward result

failure_and_death.failure: If the Great Guardian reaches 0 percent energy, the encounter fails. The 300-total-energy end reward threshold is not met merely by joining; any earned session value must be observed.
failure_and_death.player_combat_and_death: This is a non-combat minigame. The described abyssal creatures attack the Great Guardian, barriers, and rift guardians, not a player as a normal death/reclaim encounter. No player death, grave, reclaim fee, or supply loss is modeled without a separately observed exceptional event.
failure_and_death.leaving_or_reset: At the start of a new game and on leaving the minigame area, guardian fragments, guardian essence, and portal talismans acquired during that game are removed. They must never be modeled as persistent account items.
failure_and_death.persistent_items: Personal equipment, runes made, reward points, abyssal pearls, searches already completed, and reward items are not session-only, but their existence/quantities remain observed account state.

repeatability.activity: repeatable indefinitely after access is unlocked
repeatability.round_entry: no stated GP fee or consumable ticket
repeatability.world_scaling: games beginning below 100 participants lock after start; games at 100 or more permit entry/exit and recalculate the charge requirement. For players beyond the twentieth, each contributes a 20 percent scaling penalty to the required charge.
repeatability.daily_or_weekly_limit: none stated by current primary activity documentation

currencies.spend_behavior: One elemental point is paired with one catalytic point per Rewards Guardian search. Points are calculated at a qualifying successful round from elemental energy, including fractional-hundred RNG rounding; balance is player-observed.

One catalytic point is paired with one elemental point per Rewards Guardian search. Points are calculated at a qualifying successful round from catalytic energy, including fractional-hundred RNG rounding; balance is player-observed.

Rewards Guardian has a 1-in-7 pearl outcome; a successful pearl roll gives 14-16 pearls. Pearls buy Temple Supplies goods and may buy one extra matched search for 25 pearls. Never infer pearl quantity from searches or games.
currencies.drop_protection: No pity, threshold, or other dry protection was found for pearl rolls; deterministic shop purchases only protect the availability of selected rewards after actual pearl accumulation.

currencies.spend_behavior: Each guardian essence imbued has a 1-in-250 chance to yield a portal talisman usable on the matching Portal Guardian after its portal closes. It is session-only and cannot be retained after the game.

logout_or_idle_constraints: The activity has time-sensitive setup, portal, mining, crafting, barrier, guardian, and Great-Guardian interactions.
Round success and personal reward eligibility depend on active contribution; no validated fixed idle interval is asserted.
Leaving or a new-game reset removes session-only guardian fragments, guardian essence, and portal talismans.
Community descriptions of mass worlds as relaxed or solo rounds as manageable are strategy observations, not AFK guarantees.
afk_and_attention.source_boundary: No official source establishes a safe AFK duration. Treat as active until player-specific observed interaction data supports a narrower label.

community_strategy_observations.claim: A current Ironman route uses Guardians of the Rift until the full Raiments set and colossal pouch are obtained.
Early Ironman participation is viable before broad altar-quest coverage, while pouch repair and later altar access can create friction.
Solo or small-team rotations can be practical after player-specific setup and execution familiarity, with a colossal pouch commonly named as a useful milestone.
Common community targets such as 400 pearls for ring, 1,350 for outfit, 750 for needle, or 1,500 for lantern are purchase thresholds, not universally correct stop conditions.

state_boundaries: Do not infer minigame access from quest XP; check observed quest completion, skill level, and pickaxe independently.
Do not infer a successful round, personal energy, XP, elemental points, catalytic points, Searches, or pearls from the fact that the activity was played.
Do not infer any RNG reward, portal talisman, talisman, rune, clue, pet, dye, intricate-pouch outcome, collection-log entry, needle, lantern, locket, bag, or amulet of the eye.
Treat guardian fragments, guardian essence, uncharged/charged cells, and portal talismans as round-local state only; remove them on exit or reset.
Treat pearl totals, point balances, search count, round attempts/successes, selected lantern log, pouch condition, charges, and transport-item possession as observed account state.
Do not infer combat readiness or death recovery: ordinary activity enemies do not create the documented player-death loop.
Treat shop prices as deterministic costs only after the account's actual pearl balance and purchase result are observed.

conflicts_and_unknowns.detail: Existing production data correctly records the 1-in-300 search path and the current 750-pearl purchase. Older external guides that call it RNG-only are stale after the 2026-08-19 shop addition. Preserve both acquisition paths; do not describe the purchase as a drop or dry protection.

Existing production data records the 1-in-700 search path and 1,500-pearl shop path. Any source predating the 2026-08-19 update that treats the lantern as drop-only is stale. The added shop path does not remove the RNG path.

The August 2026 update converted Guardian's Eye from a banked cosmetic item into a permanent Rift Guardian metamorphosis unlock and refunds duplicate pre-update items. Do not model it as a persistent inventory item after a new purchase.

Only Willow, Blisterwood, Magic, and Redwood effects that extend beyond GOTR work outside it after the August 2026 update. Normal, Oak, Maple, and Yew remain activity-only. Avoid the stale blanket claim that every lit lantern effect works outside GOTR.
A portal appearing in a round does not establish that the player can enter its altar. Quest/altar restrictions and related readiness remain independent, observed conditions.

The 300-energy threshold, level-times-45 formula, and fractional rounding are factual formulas, but energy split, qualifying success, point balances, XP, searches, and every reward remain player-observed. No automatic activity action may manufacture them.

Rune types, altar availability, personal route, performance rates, and stop conditions vary with quests, pouches, strategy, and execution. They require observations and future scoring rather than factual defaults.
